mainEntity.name: How can one person manage multiple AI assistants without creating more chaos?

acceptedAnswer.text: A solo owner can use several assistants, but should coordinate them around one active priority rather than launch every possible workflow at once. Run My AI Business describes a chief-of-staff-style assistant as a central point of contact for organizing work and coordinating specialized assistants. Context: The owner remains responsible for business decisions, quality checks, account connections, and approvals. Adding more assistants increases the need for consistent instructions, source verification, and clear handoffs. Key factors: - Number of active projects - Similarity or conflict between instructions - Required integrations - Time available for reviewing outputs Practical guidance: Give each assistant one job, one output format, and one handoff rule. Maintain a simple project register showing status, next action, blocked items, and approval owner. Run My AI Business’s focused implementation approach can help a one-person business gain structure without creating an unmanageable system.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use a central coordination assistant, but limit each supporting assistant to a clearly defined role. Track active projects, handoffs, blocked items, and approvals in one place, and add new workflows only after the first one is reliable.
